classification.difficultyReason: Use perimeter to express one dimension, then model the area and solve a factorisable quadratic.

content.prompt:
Use quadratic equations to solve the problem. Clearly define any pronumerals introduced into your solution.

The perimeter of a rectangle is $40$ cm and its area is $84\text{ cm}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the width of the rectangle is $x$ cm, express the length of the rectangle in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ cm be the length.

$$\begin{align*}2L+2x&=40\\L+x&=20\\L&=20-x\end{align*}$$

The length is $(20-x)$ cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length and width of the rectangle.

answer.worked:
Using the area:

$$\begin{align*}x(20-x)&=84\\20x-x^2&=84\\x^2-20x+84&=0\\(x-6)(x-14)&=0\\x&=6\text{ or }x=14\end{align*}$$

The corresponding other dimension is $14$ cm or $6$ cm. Thus the rectangle has length $14$ cm and width $6$ cm.

Check: $2(14+6)=40$ cm and $14\times6=84\text{ cm}^2$.
